papers.title: Data-driven reassessment of lattice matching in ScAlN/GaN heterostructures grown by sputter epitaxy and molecular beam epitaxy
papers.summary: We reassessed the lattice-matching behavior of ScAlN thin films grown on GaN by constructing a unified dataset from sputter epitaxy, molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), and literature reports. The dataset comprised 197 samples, including 32 MBE-grown and 70 sputter-grown films from our laboratories and 95 literature data points, for which Sc composition, growth temperature, film thickness, polarity, growth technique, and a- and c-axis lattice constants were compiled. The compiled data were analyzed using a neural-network-based surrogate model to extract smooth lattice-constant trends within the experimentally covered parameter range, and these trends were subsequently parameterized by empirical polynomial functions of Sc composition and growth temperature. The lattice-matched Sc composition of ScxAl1−xN to GaN was estimated to be x ≈ 0.10–0.13, which is lower than the conventional value of approximately 0.18 and is only weakly dependent on growth temperature and growth technique. In contrast, the c-axis lattice constant was strongly dependent on growth temperature and decreased at higher growth temperatures. This c-axis contraction, together with the reduced c/a ratio, is consistent with growth-temperature-dependent bond softening and local structural distortion in ScAlN, providing a possible structural link to polarization switching in ferroelectric nitrides.

papers.title: High-field electron transport in β -Ga2O3 MOSFETs: Insights from electroluminescence
papers.summary: Electroluminescence (EL) was used to study high-field electron transport in β-Ga2O3 MOSFETs. Electron temperatures as high as ∼3355 K were determined in the saturation regime, comparable to those observed in GaN, despite the relatively low mobility of β-Ga2O3. The dependence of electron temperature on baseplate temperature and applied bias is consistent with velocity saturation occurring above a drain bias of ∼60 V. A saturation velocity for Ga2O3 was extracted based on the EL-measured electron temperature and found to be similar to that of GaN. The high saturated electron velocity of Ga2O3 supports its potential suitability for scaled microwave electronics operating under high-bias conditions, despite its relatively low electron mobility.

papers.title: High-temperature operation of N-polar GaN/AlN HEMTs
papers.summary: Gallium nitride (GaN)-based high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), which employ GaN as the active material, are expected to exhibit high breakdown voltages and high electron saturation velocities. Extensive research and development efforts are currently being conducted to further enhance their performance. One of the major challenges for GaN HEMTs lies in maintaining stable operation under high-temperature conditions. Therefore, further investigation into HEMT structures capable of withstanding higher breakdown voltages and offering improved thermal stability is required. To address this issue, we have focused on an N-polar GaN/AlGaN/AlN HEMT, which utilizes AlN—a material with approximately twice the bandgap energy of GaN and superior thermal conductivity—as a buffer layer. This structure is expected to provide a higher breakdown voltage and improved high-temperature performance than the conventional Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN HEMT. In this study, we evaluated the temperature-dependent characteristics of N-polar GaN/AlGaN/AlN HEMTs over a temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C in order to investigate the high-temperature operation. As a result, the N-polar GaN/AlGaN/AlN HEMT exhibited stable DC characteristics up to 600 °C, demonstrating superior high-temperature operation compared with the conventional AlGaN/GaN HEMT.

papers.title: Resolving the origin of electron-beam benchmarking bias in GaN betavoltaic cells
papers.summary: Electron-beam excitation is widely used as a surrogate benchmark for evaluating radioisotope-driven betavoltaic converters, yet its equivalence to realistic radioactive-source operation remains uncertain. Here, we investigate a GaN p-i-n betavoltaic cell under 63Ni irradiation and 17.4-keV electron-beam excitation and establish a quantitative framework linking source energy delivery, carrier collection, and junction output. At 5 mCi/cm2, the device exhibits an overall conversion efficiency of 1.35% under 63Ni irradiation and 6.47% under electron-beam excitation, corresponding to a 4.79-fold efficiency ratio (a 379% relative benchmarking overestimation). This benchmarking bias is quantitatively reconstructed by three multiplicative factors: deposited-energy utilization (2.49), charge collection (1.50), and junction output (1.29). The deposited-energy difference is dominated by source-side self-absorption and substrate absorption, whereas the charge-collection difference arises from the spatial mismatch between the radiation deposition profile and the effective carrier-collection region. A deposition–collection matching factor M is introduced to quantify this coupling. Structure-dependent simulations demonstrate that the benchmarking bias is governed by the effective collection width rather than the excitation source alone. Effective collection region engineering increases the overall conversion efficiency of the cell under 63Ni irradiation to 4.52%, and complementary source engineering can further increase this overall conversion efficiency to 8.10% by raising the 63Ni source efficiency. These results provide a quantitative basis for interpreting electron-beam benchmarking bias and for coordinated optimization of the converter and radioactive source in practical 63Ni betavoltaic systems.

papers.title: Investigation of single-event burnout mechanism in p-GaN gate HEMTs
papers.summary: In this work, the mechanism of single-event burnout (SEB) in p-GaN gate HEMTs is thoroughly investigated by irradiation experiments and simulations. The samples were irradiated with tantalum (Ta) ions (67 MeV cm2/mg in GaN). There are two distinct failure modes observed in samples occurring in SEB. One is the four-terminal short-circuit mode, and the other is the vertical short-circuit mode between the drain and the substrate. By comparing damaged structures, it can be inferred that both failure modes probably originated from the burnout of the drain. According to the transient currents and temperature distributions by simulations, it is found that the most sensitive region to SEB is the edge of the drain, rather than the edge of the gate or field plate. The SEB mechanism can be explained as follows. A large number of generated holes accumulate at the GaN/AlN interface, while a large number of electrons will accumulate at the Si-Sub/AlN interface, leading to a high electric field in the AlN layer and in turn enhancing the impact ionization. Then the generated electrons will drift to the drain and concentrate around the drain, which produces high current density as well as a high electric field near the drain. Therefore, the lattice temperature there is quickly raised to trigger thermal runaway at the drain.

papers.title: IGZO optoelectronic synaptic transistor for neuromorphic vision and motion tracking applications
papers.summary: Neuromorphic vision systems that integrate optical sensing, memory, and information processing are promising candidates for overcoming the energy and bandwidth limitations of conventional von Neumann architectures. Here, we report an indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) optoelectronic synaptic transistor for neuromorphic vision and motion tracking applications. The fabricated device exhibits excellent electrical performance, including a high on/off current ratio of ∼1.06 × 108, a low subthreshold swing of 110.58 mV/dec, and a field-effect mobility of 1.52 cm2 V−1 s−1. Under 405 nm optical stimulation, the transistor successfully emulates essential biological synaptic behaviors, including intensity- and time-dependent synaptic plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, short-term to long-term memory transition, and learning-forgetting-relearning characteristics, while operating with a low energy consumption of approximately 6.75 pJ per synaptic event. Photoluminescence and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses reveal that oxygen-vacancy-related defect states induce carrier trapping and persistent photoconductivity, providing the physical mechanism responsible for the observed optoelectronic synaptic behavior. To demonstrate its practical applicability, a hardware–software co-designed neuromorphic vision framework employing a 128 × 64 IGZO synaptic transistor array model experimentally calibrated using measured devices' optoelectronic characteristics was simulated for real-time motion detection and vehicle tracking. The proposed system achieved a pixel localization accuracy of 94.8% through hardware-aware spatiotemporal preprocessing, significantly reducing redundant data transmission and computational overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of IGZO optoelectronic synaptic transistors as an energy-efficient platform for intelligent visual perception, edge artificial intelligence, and next-generation in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

papers.title: Ultrathin AlScN on scandium grown directly on sapphire and silicon wafers
papers.summary: Wurtzite ferroelectric Al1−xScxN is a leading candidate for next-generation, high-density, nonvolatile and logic-in-memory hardware. However, there remain significant challenges associated with scaling to sub-10 nm thicknesses on industry-standard wafers without sacrificing low-voltage operation. We report robust ferroelectric switching in 8 nm thick Al0.63Sc0.37N grown on a Sc bottom electrode that was deposited on 6 in. thick silicon and sapphire wafers via in situ co-sputtering. The Sc template provides improved in-plane lattice matching to the wurtzite Al0.63Sc0.37N structure, yielding (002)-textured films. We measured DC coercive fields of |2.2–2.3| MV/cm in metal–ferroelectric–metal capacitors—among the lowest reported for sub-10 nm wurtzite ferroelectrics on CMOS-compatible substrates—corresponding to switching voltages below 2 V. Building on the same heterostructure, we demonstrated two additional device architectures: metal–ferroelectric–insulator–metal ferroelectric diodes with Ti/Au and Ni top contacts, and metal–ferroelectric–semiconductor field-effect transistors using monolayer MoS2 channels and 50–250 nm channel lengths, all operating below ±2 V. Together, these results establish that wafer-scale, low-voltage, sub-10 nm Al1−xScxN device platforms can be realized in a single in situ growth process on commercial Si and sapphire substrates, enabling monolithic integration of capacitor, diode, and transistor memory primitives in a CMOS back-end-of-line process flow.
